messages:
liz: Heads-up — MapleHealth onboarding is hitting 429s during browser SDK init. Spike started ~2026-03-20 10:22 PT after they enabled a service worker. Short logs attached below.

devops-bot: alert -> 429-spike detected for customer=maplehealth key=sk_live_xxx, window=2026-03-20T17:22Z, peak_rate=350r/s :rotating_light:

omar: Can you paste the SDK init snippet and confirm if they're using a service worker or server-side token minting?

liz: They are a SPA with a service worker that proxies fetch() to enable offline. Dev says SW registers on every route change in their current setup, so there may be duplicate init calls and occasional replays.

kai: Two amplifiers to check: 1) service worker replaying fetches on network events, 2) Cloudflare/edge caching of preflight/OPTIONS that strips Authorization leading to 401 -> client retry storms. :eyes:

liz: Here's the failing preflight curl we captured from their staging env (OPTIONS missing auth header):

-----
curl -i -X OPTIONS https://api.redwood.example/v1/init \
  -H "Origin: https://app.maple.example" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type"
-----

omar: If the edge responds to OPTIONS without passing Authorization, browsers may treat the CORS preflight as OK/failed in unexpected ways and your client code can retry the POST. On top of that, if their SW queues failed POSTs for later replay that doubles the requests.

santiago: Also check how they mint ephemeral keys. They were issuing a fresh ephemeral token per tab load (TTL=30s) which causes many simultaneous handshakes when tens of users reconnect. Recommend server-side mint + short reuse window (e.g., 5m) for onboarding ramp.

kai: Quick mitigations we suggested: 1) Temporarily disable the service worker for the onboarding release, 2) Configure Cloudflare to bypass caching for /v1/* and OPTIONS, or ensure Authorization is preserved (no edge-level auth strip). Also add Cache-Control: no-cache on OPTIONS responses and Vary: Authorization if needed.

liz: We walked the customer through those three changes. After CF bypass + disabling SW during rollout + switching to server-issued ephemeral token reuse, their 429s dropped to baseline within 10 minutes. They reported successful onboarding flow. :thumbsup:

omar: Nice. Can we capture a short KB note for future onboardings? Small checklist: SW double-register, CF options caching, ephemeral TTL reuse.

liz: Will do — I'll create a short KB and schedule a 30-min enablement demo with their eng lead to review best practices and capture feedback. Also adding a follow-up item for renewals team — this was a risk if not fixed.

santiago: FYI, I'll open a tiny docs PR to include a note about service workers and preflight behavior in the browser SDK guide.

liz: Thanks all — closing loop with the customer now. I'll add details into Gainsight and ping renewals.

omar: :raised_hands: great work!
